title: Write Python functions that pass their tests
summary: The model writes a Python function; an AgentCore Runtime sandbox runs it against the function's tests, and the share of tests passed is the reward. Model-written code never runs in your process, which holds your AWS credentials and the training session.

sandbox.executes: The code of each sampled answer and its tests, one microVM per answer (or per group)

evidence.basis: live run r-261110-080539-d200 of this template
evidence.note: One live run on 2026-11-10 with the defaults (6 steps, 8 functions x 4 answers, one sandbox session per answer). The sandbox side worked: 223 sessions opened and stopped, none throttled, first call p50 1.57 s, 3.8 to 4.9 s of testing per step. Training did not show: the base model already passed almost every test (mean reward 0.98 to 1.0, held-out 8 to 8), and only steps 0 and 2 had groups with a gradient, so the problems need to be harder. Training tokens $0.0144 (matches BillableTokenUsage); AgentCore Runtime $0.0304 for the 223 sessions (usage logs x list price), about twice the tokens. An earlier run that day prompted a plain Python file to continue: gpt-oss-20b wrote prose in all 192 answers, which is why the prompt uses the harmony format.

you_will_see: A fourth block on your side of the loop that runs in AgentCore Runtime, not in this process: its sessions, cold starts and AgentCore cost
A reward check in the sandbox before the training session exists: correct, wrong and broken functions, one that exits before its tests finish, one that never returns
Reward, share of bodies passing every test, share with no result, and the sandbox's cold start per step

metrics.label: Answers with no result (crash, early exit, timeout)

params.label: Test timeout (s)
params.help: Code still running after this is killed with its whole process group and scores no result. In a new sandbox version's first sessions a correct solution's test program took up to 4.9 s, and up to 6.0 s later (measured).

params.label: Sandbox per
params.help: One AgentCore Runtime session per answer, or one per group of answers for the same function, wiped between answers.

params.label: Max tokens per completion
params.help: The service minimum is 512. The model reasons briefly before it writes the code; an answer cut off before its code block scores 0.

variants.label: Share of tests passed
variants.summary: passed / total; 0 when the program left no result.
variants.watch: Answers that fail some tests still rank above ones that fail all, so more groups give a gradient.

variants.label: All or nothing
variants.summary: 1 only when every test passed in time.
variants.watch: Groups whose answers all fail at least one test give no gradient.

variants.label: Exit code only
variants.summary: 1 when the test program exits with code 0, as when grading by pytest's exit status.
variants.watch: The reward check warns: an answer that calls os._exit(0) skips the tests and still scores 1.

variants.label: One session per answer
variants.summary: Every answer gets a fresh microVM, stopped as soon as it is scored, as MTRL does per rollout.
variants.watch: The most sessions and cold starts: prompts x samples per step.

variants.label: One session per group
variants.summary: The answers for one function share a microVM; its work directory is wiped and its processes killed between answers.
variants.watch: A quarter of the sessions with 4 samples per prompt; answers of a group run one after another.
